intro: The old clockmaker left his whole bench to whichever apprentice could finish the last clock. It has no face and no hands, only fourteen drawers, and the apprentices treat it less like an inheritance than a slow trial. In the workshop the bench-keeper's habit is to keep every odd wheel and jewel in the pigeonhole cut for it, and no one has ever forced a part into a hole that shut tight. They wind the unfinished movement each morning by the light from the north window, and they leave their own tools where the last user set them down. Dust moves in the same lanes every afternoon, and the new apprentice still jumps at the sound of the regulator's release.
echo: The oldest clock in the garden is useless after dark and honest all day.

puzzles.title: Beat Error
puzzles.flavor: Everything came out of the wash with a little something extra.
hints: Each jumble is almost a word from this round, but with a letter to spare. Which letter, every time?

puzzles.title: Remontoire
puzzles.flavor: Each column remembers what it held, but not in what order.
hints: Black squares are spaces. Which two- and three-letter words fit, using only the letters each column allows?

puzzles.title: Perpetual Calendar
puzzles.flavor: It never travels in a straight line, and neither does the truth.

blocks.text: The knight sets out from d7: Nb6 Na4 Nb2 Nc4 Na3 Nb5 Nd6.

hints: Those are chess moves. Which squares does the piece land on, and what's written there?

puzzles.title: Power Reserve

blocks.text: Somewhere in here: things to do with the workshop.

hints: Once every theme word is found, is anything left unclaimed? Read it in order.

puzzles.title: Escapement
puzzles.flavor: A familiar grid, an unfamiliar alphabet.
